summary: Describes the registration procedure for SOIF template types. It is experimental.

eli5.summary: A sign-up sheet for new kinds of summary card templates, so two groups do not pick the same name.

questions: how do you register a soif template type
subtitle: A registry system for templates that describe objects in search systems.

tldr.problem: The Summary Object Interchange Format (SOIF) allows applications to define custom templates for describing resources, but without a registry of template types, different applications create conflicting definitions for the same template names.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 2656 establishes IANA as the registrar for standard SOIF template types and defines a registration procedure. Each template type must name its attributes, mark them required or optional, specify data types and values, and describe how to version templates when they change.
tldr.outcome: This procedure was experimental and has not been widely adopted. SOIF and its registry are not widely used on the modern Internet.

today: RFC 2656 is an Experimental Protocol that defines a registration procedure for SOIF template types at IANA. SOIF itself has not seen significant adoption on the modern Internet, and this registration procedure remains primarily of historical interest.

sections.title: Introduction and Background
sections.content:
The Summary Object Interchange Format (SOIF) was created by the Harvest Project in 1994 to describe resources, and it derives from earlier IETF templates and the BibTeX bibliography format. SOIF is a human-readable format where each object has a template type (a name), a URL, and a set of attribute-value pairs. Within a single application, private agreement on what attributes a template type should have works well enough, but when SOIF objects move between applications or across the Internet, interoperability becomes difficult. For instance, two applications might each define a template type called "Person", but with different sets of attributes and data types.

RFC 2655 defines the SOIF object format itself. RFC 2656 establishes a procedure to register template types with IANA so that applications can reliably understand what attributes a registered template type should contain.
sections.eli5: When people use the same kind of summary card, they need to agree on what fields it has, how big each field is, and what kind of information goes in it. This memo is about how to keep track of all those agreements in one place.

sections.title: The Registration Procedure
sections.content:
To register a SOIF template type, a registrant must submit a proposal to IANA with the following information: a proposed template type identifier; for each attribute the template may contain, the attribute name, whether it is required or optional, a description, and the data type and encoding for its values; relationships to any existing template types (Successor, Variant, or Alternate); and any special matching semantics or authentication requirements.

Template type identifiers registered with IANA must begin with the string "IANA-" to distinguish them from privately-defined types. If an attribute in a new template type exactly matches an attribute already registered in another template type, the registrant should reference the existing attribute rather than redefining it. This allows query systems to map queries across different template types.

When a template type is revised, registrants may propose a new template type with a relationship to the original (Successor, Variant, or Alternate). Attributes retained without modification should be referenced to the earlier version; modified attributes must be described as if new.
sections.eli5: To register a new card type, you write down all the fields it has, say which ones must be filled in and which are optional, describe what goes in each field, and say whether it is a new idea or a change to an old one.

sections.title: Defining Attributes
sections.content:
Attribute names in SOIF may not end with a hyphen followed by a number, because SOIF uses that convention to distinguish multiple values of the same attribute (for example, "Publisher-1", "Publisher-2", and "Publisher-3"). Names should be short and intuitive, but the description, not the name, should convey the attribute's semantic meaning, since application interfaces map these names to user-facing labels in appropriate languages.

Descriptions of attributes (whether for new ones or referenced ones) must be in English and should provide clear criteria for determining whether an object possesses the attribute. Descriptions should include at least two practical examples. The registrant must specify whether each attribute is required (meaning it must appear in every instance of the template type, though its value can be null) and the appropriate data format, character set, and encoding for its values. Special matching semantics (such as case-sensitive comparison rules) must also be specified if they are not implied by the data format.
sections.eli5: Each field on a card needs a name, a description of what it is, whether you have to fill it in, and what kind of information goes there.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: SOIF summary objects lack any built-in authentication mechanism, and the RFC notes that registrants should include authentication attributes if the template type is intended for use on the global Internet. However, template types intended only for secure environments need not include authentication attributes. A SOIF object without authentication must be treated as unreliable and should only be used in environments where other security controls prevent spoofing. Template types registered with IANA should specify whether they require authentication attributes and under what conditions.
sections.eli5: If you do not put a signature on a card, nobody can trust that it is real. So you should say whether your card type should have a signature on it.

sections.title: Status and Outcomes
sections.content:
RFC 2656 is an Experimental Protocol. It defines the registration procedure for SOIF template types. The RFC notes that the IETF was undertaking work on a more generic schema registration facility, and if that work succeeded, SOIF template registration might be migrated to it. However, neither SOIF nor the generic schema registration framework achieved widespread adoption.

Today, SOIF is not widely used on the modern Internet. The registration procedure remains documented here for historical reference, but active SOIF deployments are minimal.
sections.eli5: This was tried out as an experiment in the late 1990s, but it never became a main way that people describe things on the Internet.
